title: New Mexico v. Meta privacy-penalty ruling — Judge Francis Mathew's expected decision on New Mexico's $35–$40B ask (Cambridge Analytica case), eight days before the Q3 print
source: NEWS: re-verified independently this session (not inherited from the proposing lane's sourcing). The Santa Fe New Mexican (fetched directly, 2026-10-03, HTTP 200) reports Judge Francis Mathew, First Judicial District Court (Santa Fe, NM), did not rule at the Oct 1 hearing but "extended the deadline for the parties to file briefs on the issues until Tuesday [Oct 6], telling them he intends to have 'something' for them two weeks after that" — Oct 6 + 14 days = Oct 20, 2026, so the date is DERIVABLE FROM THE PRIMARY'S OWN QUOTE, not merely a press paraphrase of an oral statement (strengthens the proposing lane's sourcing, which had only secondary KRQE/Source NM paraphrases of "late October"). Direct fetches of krqe.com and cnbc.com both returned HTTP 403 this session (recorded in probe-ref.blocked) — WebSearch snippets of KRQE corroborate only the vaguer "by late October"/"before the end of this month" framing, never the specific day; Santa Fe New Mexican is the sole primary carrying a derivation to a specific date. Case: State of New Mexico v. Facebook Inc., N.M. Dist. Ct., No. D-101-CV-202100132. Underlying facts unchanged from the 2026-09-25 jury verdict (26 of 29 examined statements misleading, 43M+ violations of the NM Unfair Practices Act, Cambridge Analytica data-sharing) and the Oct 1 penalty hearing (NM asks $35-40B; Meta argues for a $345M-$3.45B cap and has signaled appeal regardless of outcome). Bloomberg Law's higher $219B figure is the raw statutory ceiling ($5,000/violation x ~2.1M violations, the top of a 1.3-2.1M per-statement range) that neither party has asked the court to impose — the operative argued range stays $345M-$40B, same as the proposing lane found. This is a DIFFERENT NM-Meta case and a DIFFERENT judge (Francis Mathew) than the separate youth-mental-health public-nuisance case (Judge Bryan Biedscheid, $567M abatement + prior $375M jury penalty = $942M total) tracked under meta-2026-10-28-print's own ledger — the two must not be conflated. Checked 2026-10-03.
